key_insight: NeuroGRIP refines EEG brain graphs with external medical knowledge so seizure diagnosis is more accurate and clinically plausible.
clinical_relevance: The approach may make EEG-based seizure detection more trustworthy by reducing spurious connections and grounding predictions in validated medical guidance.
method: Builds a domain-specific knowledge graph from clinical guidelines using LLM-extracted entities and relations.
Projects EEG node embeddings into the knowledge-graph semantic space to retrieve supporting relation evidence with FAISS.
Scores and prunes edges using similarity, relation type, and source reliability to remove implausible links.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved seizure detection and interpretability on TUSZ and CHB-MIT, with predictions grounded in clinically validated knowledge.
watch_item: Performance and interpretability may depend on the quality, coverage, and currency of the external knowledge base and retrieval matching.
paper_title: NeuroGRIP: Retrieval-Augmented Graph Refinement for Knowledge-Grounded EEG Seizure Diagnosis
